finding.description: For P-grid prompts with exponent 4 or 6, retain choices whose linear coefficient matches the printed constant, then choose the power fraction with no numerical numerator factor and a one-digit denominator. This identifies the answer without integrating the power term. The correct coefficient is always 1/5 or 1/7; every allowed distractor factor produces a larger numerator or a two-digit denominator. All 146 tested cases survived delivery filtering and received credit through the native grader.

finding.description: For polynomial prompts with a quadratic term, integrate only the constant, then choose the matching option with the largest absolute cubic coefficient. Six of the seven eligible incorrect divisors produce smaller coefficients than the correct 1/3. This strategy succeeds on 66/84 equally likely bank assignments (78.6%), versus 41.7% random choice after matching the constant. Fresh delivered confirmation yielded 30/35 successes (85.7%), versus a 39.5% conditional baseline. The heuristic is imperfect, but its repeatable advantage bypasses integration of the quadratic summand.
